title: A baseball in flight is not strictly ballistic, because of drag
summary: A baseball or a soccer ball pushes enough air to leave the ideal no-drag path, and a light object can settle at a terminal speed.
body: On the flight-with-drag page, updated 21 June 2024, NASA Glenn says a ball with no engine is only approximately the path of a cannon shot. A baseball or a soccer ball generates a moderate aerodynamic drag, so the path is not strictly that ideal. For a light object on the way down, weight and drag become equal and opposite. Net force and vertical acceleration are then both zero. The guide names that constant speed terminal velocity.

sources.title: Flight Equations with Drag
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 21 June 2024. Paraphrase of the baseball-not-ballistic sentence and the terminal-velocity balance of weight and drag.
